competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample asks the student to solve something about length or distance, matching the competency sentence. Seed 42 combines two lengths with 'If they are placed end to end, what is their combined length in cm?' and answers 29; seed 46 takes a difference with 'How many cm longer is a pencil than a ruler?' and answers 4; seed 601 chooses a unit with 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the school and the market: centimeters or meters?'. Each item is answerable from the numbers printed in its own stem, with a unique correct value.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both halves of the sentence appear. Length of objects is covered by seeds 42 to 502; distance is covered by seed 601 and by seed 603 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 20 cm.'. The sub-skills span joining (seed 43, answer 38), comparing by difference (seed 50, answer 8), direct comparison in seed 602 'Which is longer: 13 cm or 6 cm?', equality in seed 606 'Segment A is 2 cm long.', unit choice, and conversion in seed 604 'Convert 4 m to cm.'.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Arithmetic stays inside Grade 2 Quarter 2 reach: single-step sums and differences with totals no larger than the 130 of seed 500, and one memorised metric relation in seed 604 'Convert 4 m to cm.' whose answer 400 rests on the known 1 m to 100 cm fact rather than on formal multiplication. No item requires more than one operation or any vocabulary past centimetre and metre.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three formatters appear across the sixteen seeds (mcq at seed 42, cloze at seed 50, read_mcq at seed 55) and the stems take six genuinely different shapes rather than one template: end-to-end joining, longer-than differencing, bare comparison, landmark distance comparison, unit selection, and metric conversion. Distractors sit one or two units either side of the key, so seed 501 with answer 18 punishes an off-by-one rather than rewarding a guess.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing reaches past the sentence. No item mentions perimeter, area, multiplication of measures, or millimetres and kilometres; the widest reach is seed 604 'Convert 4 m to cm.', which is still squarely a length question. Seed 606 answers 'Yes' about two equal segments and stays inside comparison of lengths, so the node addresses the competency without exceeding it.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Most nouns carry believable sizes: a pencil at 20 cm, a crayon at 9 cm, a ruler at 15 cm and a book at 18 cm are all right for the objects named, and centimetres suit every one of them. Three samples do not hold up. Seed 44 states 'A garden path is 30 cm long.' and pairs it end to end with a 6 cm crayon; seed 500 states 'A garden path is 100 cm long.'; no real garden path is a hand-span or a single metre long, and a path belongs in metres. Seed 603 states 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 20 cm.', which puts a bench inside the trunk, and it contradicts seed 601 in this same node, which teaches that a distance between two places is measured in 'm'. The mathematics in all three is correct and answerable, but the object-to-unit pairing has not been fixed for the garden path or the bench-to-tree distance.
